correctness.rationale: For fixed demand cardinality r>=2, n>=m and unit-supply binary perfect complements: Step 1 proves duplicate-demand satisfaction violates envy; Step 2 maps all satisfied agents to disjoint unique requests; Step 3 constructs a complete envy-free allocation for every unique-request packing by assigning unused goods separately to unused agents. The matching/3-set-packing complexity boundary follows from polynomial padding that preserves the optimum. An exact factorial-moment computation and an O(1/m) collision bound prove the Poisson welfare law and convergence of the mean. Step 8 verifies the one-sided threshold using first and second moments. Independent direct-enumeration algorithms agreed on 10862 finite demand profiles and six exact occupancy cases; no finite checks are asserted as asymptotic proofs.

originality.rationale: The main new statement connects complete envy-free welfare of identical-cardinality single-minded complement demanders to the packing of uniquely occurring requests; the exact two-vs-three complexity boundary and Poisson extinction law are consequences for the same allocation objective. The initiating 2026 Leontief paper states general hardness and tractable one-good/identical-demand cases and primarily assumes positive demand for every type; our model explicitly permits zero demand outside the requested set. Classical graph matching, 3-dimensional matching, and occupancy alone do not imply the envy-free packing equivalence. Available claim databases and targeted primary-literature searches yielded no clear dominating statement; inaccessible material and unindexed equivalents remain a real priority risk.
residual_risks: Full proof sections and appendices of arxiv:2609.28308 were not accessible despite direct and alternate lawful access attempts. This limits completeness of the same-object literature comparison.
An earlier single-minded-allocation theorem or an unpublished/unindexed preprint could already imply the exact packing identity.
The occupancy limit is a standard type of Poisson approximation; novelty is claimed for its welfare interpretation and the exact structural connection, not for the general factorial-moment method.

value.rationale: Motivated by difficult complete envy-free welfare maximization for indivisible complementary resources. A natural unit-supply equal-cardinality class admits an exact optimizable invariant once singleton parking is available; r=2 versus every fixed r>=3 marks a nontrivial polynomial/NP-complete boundary. Independent uniform demands cause a counterintuitive crowd-out transition: increasing participation eventually drives the optimal fair welfare to zero, with an exact finite probability and universal limiting Poisson law. This gives a precise benchmark for complementary resource allocation, not an arbitrary tiny numerical slice.
